bottom_line: Compared with placebo, dabigatran was associated with higher major or clinically relevant minor bleeding, with hazard ratio (HR) 4.27 (1.86, 9.81) for 150 mg.
implications: These data support that adding dabigatran to predominantly dual antiplatelet therapy increased the 6-month risk of major or clinically relevant minor bleeding in a dose-dependent fashion (e.g., HR 4.27 [1.86, 9.81] at 150 mg vs placebo). The trial reports numerically similar or lower rates of the composite of cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, or non-haemorrhagic stroke at higher doses (3.0% and 3.5% at 110 and 150 mg vs 3.8% placebo), but ischaemic endpoints were reported descriptively, so definitive efficacy conclusions are not licensed by these numbers alone.

major_points.text: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, dose-escalation trial in acute myocardial infarction patients largely on dual antiplatelet therapy.
major_points.quote: In this double-blind, placebo-controlled, dose-escalation trial, 1861 patients (99.2% on dual antiplatelet treatment)

major_points.text: Patients were enrolled a mean of 7.5 days after ST-elevation or non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction and randomized to four dabigatran doses or placebo twice daily.
major_points.quote: enrolled at mean 7.5 days (SD 3.8) after an ST-elevation (60%) or non-ST-elevation (40%) myo- cardial infarction and randomized to twice daily treatment with dabigatran 50 mg (n ¼ 369), 75 mg (n ¼ 368), 110 mg (n ¼ 406), 150 mg (n ¼ 347), or placebo (n ¼ 371).

major_points.text: Primary endpoint was major or clinically relevant minor bleeding during the 6-month treatment period.
major_points.quote: Primary outcome was the composite of major or clinically rel- evant minor bleeding during the 6-month treatment period.

major_points.text: There was a dose-dependent increase in primary bleeding outcome versus placebo, with HR 3.92 (1.72, 8.95) for 110 mg and HR 4.27 (1.86, 9.81) for 150 mg.
major_points.quote: hazard ratio (HR) 3.92 (1.72, 8.95) for 110 mg; and HR 4.27 (1.86, 9.81) for 150 mg.

major_points.text: D-dimer concentrations were reduced in all dabigatran dose groups at weeks 1 and 4 versus placebo.
major_points.quote: Compared with placebo, D-dimer concentrations were reduced in all dabigatran dose groups by an average of 37 and 45% at weeks 1 and 4, respectively (P , 0.001).

absolute_effects.text: Primary outcome (major or clinically relevant minor bleeding): 8 (2.2) placebo vs 27 (7.8) dabigatran 150 mg.
Composite cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, or non-haemorrhagic stroke: 14 (3.8) placebo vs 12 (3.5) dabigatran 150 mg.
All-cause death: 14 (3.8) placebo vs 7 (2.0) dabigatran 150 mg.
Major (ISTH definition): 2 (0.5) placebo vs 4 (1.2) dabigatran 150 mg.

subgroups.quote: Age, gender, body mass index, renal function, ethnicity, haemoglobin at baseline, and diabetes mellitus were pre-defined subgroups, and revasculariza- tion for index event was added post hoc.

subgroups.text: Female gender and age >75 years had higher bleeding incidences in the 110 and 150 mg groups, with significant treatment by subgroup interactions.
subgroups.quote: Female gender and age .75 years were associated with higher bleeding incidences in the 110 and 150 mg dose groups, with significant treatment by subgroup interactions.

harms.text: Primary outcome (major or clinically relevant minor bleeding) occurred in 2.2% placebo vs 7.9% (110 mg) and 7.8% (150 mg).
Two fatal bleeding events occurred: one in placebo and one in 110 mg group.
harms.quote: There were two fatal bleeding events, one in the placebo group and one in the 110 mg dose group.

harms.text: Most frequently reported bleeding events included gastrointestinal bleeds and epistaxis with percentages by group.
harms.quote: The most frequently reported bleeding events were gastrointes- tinal bleeds (placebo, 1.3%; 50 mg, 2.4%; 75 mg, 3.0%; 110 mg, 4.9%; 150 mg, 3.2%) and epistaxis (placebo, 0.8%; 50 mg, 3.3%; 75 mg, 2.2%; 110 mg, 4.2%; 150 mg, 3.7%).

harms.text: No intracranial or intraspinal bleeding events were observed in any group.
harms.quote: There were no intra-cranial or intra-spinal bleeding events in any of the treatment groups.
